title: Heralds of Creation! Cry
description: Heralds of Creation! Cry in Tonic Solfa to PLEYEL'S HYMN, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 465, “Praise Ye the Lord”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7) (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to PLEYEL'S HYMN; any other Sevens (7.7.7.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Her-alds of cre-a-tion! cry, Praise the Lord, the Lord most high! Heaven and earth! o-bey the call; Praise the Lord, the Lord of all.

lines: Heralds of creation! cry, —
Praise the Lord, the Lord most high!
Heaven and earth! obey the call;
Praise the Lord, the Lord of all.
For He spake, and forth from night
Sprang the universe to light;
He commanded, — nature heard,
And stood fast upon His word.
Praise Him, all ye hosts above;
Spirits perfected in love!
Sun and moon! your voices raise;
Sing, ye stars! your Maker's praise.
Earth! from all thy depths below,
Ocean's hallelujahs flow;
Lightning, vapor, wind, and storm,
Hail and snow! His will perform.
Birds! on wings of rapture soar,
Warble at His temple's door;
Joyful sounds from herds and flocks,
Echo back, ye caves and rocks!
High above all height His throne;
Excellent His name alone;
Him let all His works confess!
Him let all His children bless!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to PLEYEL'S HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
